title: LP Team
field: linear programming solver engineering, centred on the revised simplex method and above all the dual revised simplex method (pricing and CHUZR, bound-flipping ratio tests, dual steepest edge, sparse LU factorization and its updates, hyper-sparsity, parallel simplex) as built into research and production LP solvers; interior-point / barrier, first-order (PDLP-type) LP, crossover, presolve-centred and MIP traditions are not yet represented by a member
chase_hints: Optimization Online (optimization-online.org)
arXiv math.OC
University of Edinburgh: ERGO technical reports on Julian Hall's pages (webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/hall/) and the Edinburgh Research Archive (era.ed.ac.uk)
solver documentation and open source (HiGHS: github.com/ERGO-Code/HiGHS, ergo-code.github.io/HiGHS; COPT: guide.coap.online/copt/en-doc/; COIN-OR Clp; FICO Xpress manuals)
Hans Mittelmann's benchmark pages (plato.asu.edu/bench.html) for solver context only, never as the member's own words

card_dimensions.D3: problem class and data model: the LP form handled (bounded variables, computational form, slack basis), the sparsity / structure / scale properties of the instances that the technique relies on or exploits (hyper-sparsity, density, block structure), and the assumptions stated for any correctness argument
card_dimensions.D4: algorithm and implementation design: data structures and linear-algebra kernels (sparse LU factorization, FTRAN / BTRAN, basis-update schemes), pivoting and pricing rules (CHUZR, CHUZC, dual steepest edge), numerical safeguards (tolerances, Harris and bound-flipping ratio tests, perturbation), task decomposition for parallelism, and any proof or invariant together with the device used
card_dimensions.D5: computational evaluation: test set, baselines (named solvers and versions), metrics (iterations, time, geometric-mean speed-up, performance profiles), hardware and thread counts, and whether failures or slowdowns are reported

members.name: Qi Huangfu
members.hint: University of Edinburgh PhD 2013, thesis 'High performance simplex solver' (advisor J. A. J. Hall); original author of HSOL, the dual revised simplex code that became the simplex core of HiGHS; PAMI / SIP parallel dual simplex (Huangfu & Hall, Mathematical Programming Computation 2018) and LU-update techniques (Huangfu & Hall, Computational Optimization and Applications 2015); later implemented PAMI in the FICO Xpress simplex solver and develops COPT (Cardinal Optimizer, Cardinal Operations). Not the medical researchers named Qi Huangfu at Zhejiang University

members.name: John J. H. Forrest
members.hint: Simplex-code author: wrote COIN-OR Clp (primal and dual simplex, first commit 2002-07-30), Abc/Aboca (parallel dual, 2012) and CoinUtils' CoinFactorization; Forrest-Tomlin basis update (Math. Programming 1972), Forrest-Goldfarb steepest edge (Math. Programming 1992), Sprint (sifting) and the Idiot crash; earlier Scicon Ltd (UMPIRE 1974) and IBM Research (YKTLP/OSL with J. A. Tomlin; retired, date unknown, between 2006 and 2010); founding 'Benevolent Dictator' of COIN-OR. CODE-FIRST LENS, on the pattern of andreas-wachter (product/nonlinear-team: Ipopt code plus 681 mailing-list answers) and michael-powell (product/dfo-team: Fortran code and cover notes): his papers are few and all co-authored, so the primary evidence is the Clp, Abc and CoinUtils source, about ten first-person design notes in it, the commit history, his 461 GitHub issue and PR comments (2017-11-20 to 2026-11-01) and the 1998 Anbil-Forrest-Pulleyblank ICM chapter. AUTHORSHIP LABELS THAT MUST SURVIVE INTO THE SKILL: his code authorship covers Clp, Abc and CoinFactorization only; OSL, LAMPS and UMPIRE are credit by others (no code of his visible; the OSL factorization in CoinUtils is a 2009 port of IBM code, and its first-person lines read as a porter's); not all of Clp is his (ClpPdco: Tomlin; ClpPE*: Omer and Towhidi; some presolve comments read as other hands). The GitHub accounts johnjforrest (2002-2020, fastercoin.com email) and jjhforrest (2020-) are linked to him by strong inference (same display name, hand-over 2020-05-11/12, JJHF-signed comments), not by any document. 'living' rests on that account activity (latest 2026-11-01). OpenAlex: pin author A5061258306 (a name search returns other people). Name forms: John J. Forrest, J. J. H. Forrest, John Forrest; not Jeffrey Yi-Lin Forrest or other Forrests.

members.name: Robert E. Bixby
members.hint: Rice University mathematician who wrote the original CPLEX simplex code and co-founded CPLEX Optimization (1987/88) and later Gurobi (2008). SCOPE OF THIS LENS: 1987-2002 and DECISION AND MEASUREMENT CRAFT ONLY (what to build next in a production simplex code, how to measure it on real customer models, how to read version-to-version and algorithm-to-algorithm comparisons), from these primary sources: 'Solving Real-World Linear Programs: A Decade and More of Progress', Operations Research 50(1):3-15, 2002 (DOI 10.1287/opre.50.1.3.17780); 'A Brief History of Linear and Mixed-Integer Programming Computation', Documenta Math. Extra Vol. ISMP 2012, 107-121; the Optima 101 interview (questions October 2015, issue September 2016); ZIB SC 92-11 'Das Implementieren des Simplex-Verfahrens: Die Startbasis' (German, April 1992; English version ORSA J. Comput. 4(3):267-284, 1992); ZIB SC-95-45, Bixby and Martin, 'Parallelizing the Dual Simplex Method' (December 1995 preprint; published INFORMS J. Comput. 12(1):45-56, 2000); and the September 2022 Hausdorff School deck 'Linear Programming: A Historical View'. Of his other works, only the LP subset counts (initial basis, the 1992 interior-point and simplex case study with sifting, the 1994 commentary 'Progress in Linear Programming', basis recovery from an interior point, embedded network rows); matroid, TSP and MIP work is context only. AUTHORSHIP LABELS THAT MUST SURVIVE INTO THE SKILL: his authorship stops at his own statements: the main parts of the CPLEX simplex as of April 1992 (SC 92-11, printed p. 2), all development at the 1988 first release (Optima 101 p. 3), still doing development in 1997 (Optima 101 p. 4), and no development at Gurobi (Optima 101 pp. 4-5). Later CPLEX changes (5.0 to 7.1 and after) are not shown to be his: OR 2002 p. 14 credits Gu, Lustig, Rothberg and Wunderling with fundamental contributions to the LP algorithms. Dual steepest edge is Forrest and Goldfarb's method that CPLEX implemented, by his own texts. LIVING STATUS AND PRESENT ROLE ARE NOT ESTABLISHED by any dated source after September 2022 (the Hausdorff deck is the latest dated trace; Rothberg became Gurobi chairman on 2 January 2023): the 'living' key is deliberately left out of this entry until the user decides; the skill must not state either. OpenAlex author A5012463224.
